signals.title: AUD/USD — Inflation Miss + Geopolitical Shock + Vol
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.6948 following a sharp depreciation triggered by Australian June CPI missing expectations at 3.8% vs 4.0% forecasted. This disinflationary data cools RBA hike expectations just as geopolitical tensions escalate, with Iran's Revolutionary Guards reportedly hitting three oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz. The AUD/USD 25d RR at -0.81 confirms an options bias for downside protection, while the AUD/USD VRP of +8.4% (IV 14.6% vs HV30 6.2%) indicates extreme hedging demand against realized volatility. Technically, the pair is testing its SMA20 at 0.6962 from below, with a failure to reclaim this level opening a path toward the SMA200 at 0.6904. The combination of cooling domestic carry support and rising Middle East risk-off flows creates a significant headwind for the pro-cyclical AUD. RBA holds at 4.35%.
evidence: Strait of Hormuz: 3 tankers hit (State TV)

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry vs Intervention + Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 163.71, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (162.50/161.15/157.78) as a 275bp Fed-BoJ holds at 1.0%. Despite the spot strength, the 25d RR at -1.49 shows a moderate put skew, signaling that the options market is paying a premium for JPY strength protection against BoJ intervention risks near 165.00. COT data shows a crowded JPY net short at -114,030, leaving the pair vulnerable to a disorderly unwind if the BoJ delivers a hawkish surprise or intervention occurs. The divergence between spot carry demand and defensive options positioning suggests institutional participants are hedging for a volatility spike. Risk: BoJ maintains a dovish hold on July 31, validating the carry trade and clearing the path to 165.00.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Positioning + ESI + Vol Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD is trading at 1.1395, positioned below its SMA20/50/200 cluster (1.1417/1.1496/1.1637), confirming a medium-term bearish technical regime. Speculative positioning is significantly stretched with EUR COT LF net short at -80,570 (long%=32.4%), aligning with a negative ESI of -9.2 which reflects consistent misses in Eurozone data. However, the EUR/USD VRP of +2.5% (IV 7.1% vs HV30 4.6%) suggests the options market is pricing in more volatility than realized, likely due to the +135bp USD carry advantage and upcoming FOMC risks. While the negative sentiment is well-entrenched, the heavy short positioning creates an asymmetric risk to the upside on any hawkish ECB shift or USD weakness. Risk: ECB signals a pause in its hiking cycle on September 10, validating the fundamental short bias.

signals.title: USD/CHF — Vol Extreme + Retail Divergence
signals.text: USD/CHF trades at 0.8185, currently positioned above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.8095/0.8009/0.7922), supported by a massive +375bp Fed-SNB carry advantage. The pair exhibits an extreme Vol Risk Premium of +22.0% (IV 27.8% vs HV30 5.8%), the highest in the G10 space, suggesting an acute pricing of tail-risk moves despite a stable spot trend. Retail sentiment is 68% short, diverging from the prevailing technical uptrend and institutional carry logic, which typically serves as a contrarian signal for further upside. While the SNB remains on hold at 0.00%, the restrictive US real rate of +1.59% vs the Swiss real rate of -0.03% provides a structural floor for the pair. Risk: Escalation in Middle East tensions triggers a surge in safe-haven demand, compressing the carry-driven bid.
